xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5168: macOS: pollers that run missing binaries create ~10 dead processes per call (spawn storm, up to ~60/s)

plan.title: macOS: pollers that run missing binaries create ~10 dead processes per call (spawn storm, up to ~60/s)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: Nine small vertical slices over one shared module; 20 files and 5 subsystems (lib, dashboard server, cli, tests, docs).

narratives.Problem: On macOS, Node's libuv tries posix_spawn once per PATH entry for a bare command name, and XNU creates a short-lived process for each try. Pollers that run a missing docker or tmux on a fixed interval therefore create about 10 dead processes per call. An idle dashboard with no Docker and no tmux created 13-20 processes per second, and about 60 per second with many conversations. Verified pollers: the two DockerStatsCollector instances (docker stats + docker ps every 5 s each), resource discovery's loadDockerContainers, the stack-health lifecycle snapshot, the runtime census's tmux list-panes (3 s TTL), and the conversation-liveness tmux fallback (once per conversation per poll under herdr).
narratives.Proposal: Add src/lib/host-tools.ts: a synchronous, spawn-free, cached PATH lookup built on findExecutableOnPath. A found tool stays cached until refreshHostTools() or a spawn ENOENT that a fresh lookup confirms. A missing tool is cached as null and looked up again (no spawn) every 60 s. Pollers call resolveHostTool before they spawn, skip the tick when it returns null, spawn the resolved absolute path (docker), and pass spawn errors to noteHostToolSpawnFailed. Gates go into the five pollers only (docker stats, resource discovery, stack health, runtime census, conversation-liveness tmux helpers), never into tmuxExecAsync or systemctl(). pan doctor prints a Host tools row from a fresh lookup. PUT /api/settings re-checks through a new applySavedSettings helper, which also shrinks the capped settings.ts route file. Tests keep their behavior through OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS=1 set in tests/setup.ts, plus a per-test finder override that each test file resets in its own afterEach; tests/setup.ts imports nothing from src/.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Routing conversation pane reads (capturePane, readConversationInputTarget, conversationNeedsTerminal) away from tmux under herdr — PAN-5169 owns it
- Changing ensureHostTools, isToolInstalled, or brew install behavior in src/lib/prereqs/registry.ts — PAN-5169 owns it
- Platform guards for systemctl (src/lib/systemd.ts) and the journalctl OOM canary (src/lib/cloister/memory-pressure-patrol.ts) — PAN-5170 owns them
- A second tool cache or a second PATH lookup helper anywhere
- Gating tmuxExecAsync, systemctl(), or any agent/conversation launch path; src/lib/tmux.ts is not edited; only the five named pollers are gated
- Gating on-demand docker calls (workspace create/remove, container and prune routes, doctor's own docker checks)
- Gating the deacon hygiene patrols (idle-stack-reaper.ts, bridge-pool-patrol.ts, merged-docker-reconcile.ts): they run docker through a shell every 60 s or slower, so each call costs about one process
- Changing herdr probing, backend selection, or the legacy-tmux fallback in conversation-liveness.ts beyond the missing-tool gate
- Merging the two DockerStatsCollector singletons into one
- Handling a docker CLI that is present while the daemon is down
- Handling a binary that is on PATH but fails exec with ENOENT (for example a broken shebang interpreter)
- A dashboard HTTP route that lets pan doctor reset the server's cache
- Switching tmux spawns to absolute paths
- Raising any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt cap

autoDecisions.summary: Build the lookup on findExecutableOnPath (src/lib/pan-cli-shim.ts), not resolveExecutableDetailed (src/lib/harness-binary.ts).
autoDecisions.rationale: resolveExecutableDetailed spawns npm prefix -g and a login shell on a miss, which is the cost this issue removes; a PATH-only lookup matches what libuv's spawn would find.

autoDecisions.summary: Missing tools are looked up again on a fixed 60 s interval (stat only, no spawn); a found tool stays cached until refreshHostTools() or a confirmed ENOENT.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks to resolve once, skip missing tools, and back off after ENOENT. A PATH lookup costs a few stat calls, so a fixed interval is cheap and lets a newly installed tool appear within a minute without an exponential schedule.

autoDecisions.summary: An ENOENT marks a tool missing only when a fresh PATH lookup also misses.
autoDecisions.rationale: Node reports a missing cwd as 'spawn <cmd> ENOENT' too; marking the tool missing on that error would suppress a tool that exists.

autoDecisions.summary: pan doctor's re-check is its own fresh lookup through the shared module (a Host tools row); no HTTP route resets the dashboard's cache.
autoDecisions.rationale: The doctor CLI, the dashboard server, and the deacon child are separate processes. A route would add route-scope and no-loss-matrix work for little value, because the dashboard re-checks missing tools every 60 s on its own.

autoDecisions.summary: The settings-change re-check runs on PUT /api/settings through a new services/settings-saved.ts helper that also holds the route's three existing post-save calls.
autoDecisions.rationale: routes/settings.ts is at its file-size cap (1104/1104), so it cannot gain an import; folding the calls into a helper shrinks it.

autoDecisions.summary: The tmux gates go into the runtime census's default listPanes and the default tmux helpers of conversation-liveness.ts, not into tmuxExecAsync.
autoDecisions.rationale: tmux.ts is at its cap (1167/1167), tmuxExecAsync also serves launch paths, and PAN-5169 owns the conversation pane reads. The census is the remaining tmux poller under herdr, and a rejected listPanes keeps today's tmuxAvailable:false semantics. The liveness fallback asks tmux once per conversation per poll under herdr; with tmux missing no tmux session can exist, so answering false without a spawn is exact.

autoDecisions.summary: Tests keep their behavior through OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS=1 in tests/setup.ts (no src/ import there) plus setHostToolFinderForTests for missing-tool cases, which each test file resets in its own afterEach.
autoDecisions.rationale: CI's test shards do not install tmux, and many tests mock child_process for tmux/docker; a real PATH lookup would skip their mocked spawns. An env var survives vi.resetModules(), unlike module state, and matches the existing OVERDECK_TERMINAL_BACKEND test default.

autoDecisions.summary: Docker pollers spawn the resolved absolute path; tmux stays spawned by bare name.
autoDecisions.rationale: The absolute path also removes libuv's per-PATH-entry failed tries when docker is present. Other tmux command lines (pty.spawn, Herdr) use the bare name, so tmux stays consistent with them.

autoDecisions.summary: HostToolName includes systemctl, journalctl, and brew, but PAN-5168 wires only docker and tmux call sites.
autoDecisions.rationale: The coordination comment names those tools for the shared module so PAN-5169/PAN-5170 can adopt it later; their call sites belong to those sibling issues.

items.title: Add src/lib/host-tools.ts cached spawn-free PATH lookup with the test seam

verify_commands: npx vitest run tests/unit/lib/host-tools.test.ts tests/unit/lib/runtime-census.test.ts tests/unit/cli/doctor-pan-path.test.ts
expected_outputs: host-tools.test.ts passes all eleven cases; runtime-census.test.ts and doctor-pan-path.test.ts still pass with the new env default
metadata.acJustification: Six criteria: the foundation carries the cache, ENOENT, error-shape, env-seam, real-PATH and setup/circularity checks that every downstream gate depends on.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-1 exactly. Create src/lib/host-tools.ts that exports: type HostToolName = 'docker'|'tmux'|'systemctl'|'journalctl'|'brew'; HOST_TOOL_MISSING_RECHECK_MS = 60_000; interface HostToolDeps { find?, pathEnv?, now? }; resolveHostTool(name, deps?) returning string|null; noteHostToolSpawnFailed(name, error, deps?); refreshHostTools(); isSpawnNotFoundError(error) (walks .cause up to 4 levels: code === 'ENOENT', or reason._tag === 'NotFound'); hostToolNotFoundError(name), a Node-shaped ENOENT error with code/errno/syscall/path; setHostToolFinderForTests(find|null), which also clears the cache; resetHostToolsForTests(). Cache entries are keyed by tool name and store {path, pathEnv, recheckAt}; an entry whose pathEnv differs from the current PATH is stale. Lookup precedence: deps.find, then the test finder, then OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS === '1' (returns the bare name), then findExecutableOnPath(name, pathEnv) from ./pan-cli-shim.js. noteHostToolSpawnFailed ignores non-ENOENT errors; on ENOENT it deletes the entry and calls resolveHostTool again, so the tool is marked missing only when the fresh lookup misses. Import only ./pan-cli-shim.js. The module is plain sync code with no Effect. In tests/setup.ts set process.env.OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS = '1' next to the OVERDECK_TERMINAL_BACKEND default, with a PAN-5168 comment. Do NOT add any src/ import to tests/setup.ts. Each test file that calls setHostToolFinderForTests resets in its own afterEach. Write the eleven tests named in PRD WI-1: nine use injected find/pathEnv/now (no real waits); two exercise the real findExecutableOnPath route with vi.stubEnv('OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS', '') against a fresh mkdtempSync directory (empty -> null; with an 0o755 file named docker -> join(dir, 'docker')). Error shapes were verified during planning: Effect.runPromise rejects with the TmuxError itself (.cause.code === 'ENOENT'), and a failed ChildProcess.make spawn rejects with a PlatformError whose reason._tag === 'NotFound' and .cause.code === 'ENOENT'.

items.title: Given a finder that returns null, when resolveHostTool('docker', {find, now}) runs at now=0, 59999 and 60000, then it returns null each time and the finder is called once by 59999 and twice at 60000

Given a found tool, when noteHostToolSpawnFailed receives a Node ENOENT and the fresh lookup returns null, then the next resolveHostTool returns null; when the fresh lookup still finds the tool, it returns the path; a non-ENOENT error leaves the cached path untouched
isSpawnNotFoundError returns true for an Effect PlatformError.systemError with _tag 'NotFound' and for a TmuxError whose cause has code 'ENOENT', and returns false for { code: 1 }
Given OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS=1 and no injected finder, resolveHostTool('tmux') returns the bare string 'tmux'; refreshHostTools() causes the next call to invoke the finder again

Given OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS is stubbed to '' and no finder is injected, when resolveHostTool('docker', { pathEnv: <empty temp dir> }) runs it returns null, and after an executable file named docker is written into that dir and refreshHostTools() runs it returns join(dir, 'docker')
tests/setup.ts sets OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS to '1' and imports nothing from src/, setHostToolFinderForTests clears the cache, and npm run lint:circular exits 0 with the new module

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-2. In runDockerForOutput (src/lib/docker-stats.ts), call resolveHostTool('docker') at the start of each call. narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-6. Create src/cli/commands/doctor-host-tools.ts exporting checkHostTools(deps?: HostToolDeps): CheckResult, using the local CheckResult interface pattern from src/cli/commands/doctor-grok.ts. It calls refreshHostTools(), then resolveHostTool for docker, tmux, systemctl, journalctl and brew, and returns { name: 'Host tools', status: 'ok', message }. The message lists each tool as '<name> <path>' or '<name> missing', joined by ', '. When any tool is missing, it appends ' — dashboard pollers skip missing tools and look again every 60 s.' In collectDoctorChecks in src/cli/commands/doctor.ts, add 'checks.push(checkHostTools()); // PAN-5168' right after the optional-commands loop, plus the import. Leave the existing checkCommand rows unchanged.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-8. (1) docs/DASHBOARD-ARCHITECTURE.md: append a section '## Optional host tools (PAN-5168)'. It explains the macOS failed-spawn cost (one process per PATH entry), names src/lib/host-tools.ts and its exports, the five gated pollers (DockerStatsCollector, resource-discovery loadDockerContainers, stack-health collectDockerContainerLifecycleSnapshot, runtime census listHostTmuxPanes, and the conversation-liveness default tmux helpers), the 60 s re-check for missing tools, the rule that an ENOENT marks a tool missing only when a fresh lookup also misses, the per-process cache, the settings-save and pan doctor re-checks, the OVERDECK_TEST_ASSUME_HOST_TOOLS test seam, and the rule that a new poller calls resolveHostTool before spawning and noteHostToolSpawnFailed on error. (2) reference/troubleshooting.mdx: add '## Docker or tmux installed, but the dashboard still shows nothing', saying the dashboard looks again within 60 s or after a settings save, and that pan doctor's 'Host tools' row shows what this machine resolves. (3) changelog.d/pan-5168.md: one '#### Fixed' heading with one bullet: an idle dashboard on a Mac without Docker or tmux no longer creates a stream of short-lived processes, linking [#5168](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/5168); follow changelog.d/README.md formatting. (4) .overdeck/context/codebase/concerns.md: add one bullet that optional host tools resolve through src/lib/host-tools.ts and that a poller spawning a bare missing command on macOS creates ~10 processes per call (PAN-5168); keep the single <!-- last-verified: --> line unchanged at the end of the file.
